name: Computer Vision
certifications: Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer
AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate

beginner.summary: For Python programmers who are new to image processing and computer vision. Covers images as NumPy arrays, colour spaces, thresholding, filtering, edges, contours, video I/O, feature matching, homography, camera calibration, classical detectors, dataset formats, CNN basics in PyTorch, training and transfer learning, classification metrics, simple OCR, pretrained YOLO inference, and an inspection-pipeline capstone.
prerequisites: Writes Python scripts with functions, lists and NumPy arrays
Uses a terminal, pip and virtual environments
Knows high-school linear algebra: vectors, matrices and coordinates
outcomes: Load, transform, filter and analyse images and video with OpenCV
Match features, align images and calibrate a camera
Train and evaluate an image classifier with PyTorch transfer learning
Run pretrained YOLO and OCR models and package results as a command-line tool

intermediate.summary: For practitioners who can train a classifier and now need detection, segmentation, tracking, OCR, video, 3D and vision-language work. Covers augmentation, vision transformers, embeddings and retrieval, detection metrics, YOLO training, error analysis, DETR-family detectors, U-Net and instance segmentation, SAM, tracking, pose, OCR engines, optical flow, depth, structure from motion, anomaly detection, VLMs, open-vocabulary detection, and an analytics capstone.
prerequisites: Has trained a CNN classifier in PyTorch and can read training curves
Can use Git, the command line and a GPU notebook or workstation
Understands IoU, precision, recall and confusion matrices
outcomes: Train and evaluate detection and segmentation models with correct metrics
Combine detection, tracking and zone logic into video analytics
Use foundation models for embeddings, segmentation, grounding and question answering
Reconstruct depth and 3D structure from images and video

advanced.summary: For engineers who ship vision systems to production and the edge. Covers ONNX and TensorRT export, quantisation, Jetson and low-power hardware, mobile and browser inference, distillation, VLM fine-tuning, document AI, synthetic data, dataset curation, robustness, multi-camera pipelines, SLAM, radiance fields, LiDAR fusion, Triton serving, privacy and compliance, monitoring, and an edge-to-cloud capstone.
prerequisites: Has trained and evaluated detection or segmentation models
Comfortable with Docker, Linux and basic GPU tooling
Understands precision, latency and throughput trade-offs
outcomes: Export, optimise and benchmark vision models for GPU, edge and browser targets
Fine-tune and evaluate vision-language and document models
Run, monitor and retrain vision systems with drift alerts
Meet privacy, robustness and fairness requirements with documented evidence
